output.name: Telun
output.myth: Aun tied the first knot in the Lamp Road's cord the day he wondered how many days a pair of hands could work before they gave out. So he tied one knot for every day of the year's labour and strung them on a belt across the road. Mother Hesk watched from the Spindle and said nothing, which was how she scolded. He cut the belt loose and it went up and became Telun, the Knot Belt. Up in the north the Lamp-Petrel watches the storm-birds' cliff nests, where Hesk once counted the chicks with a knot in her cord. Low in the south-east the Bailer lies, and the old women say its knots are for the hands that bailed brown water in the thaw. Each festival one knot is untied so the count can be seen going down. Sil searches the road for the loose end every night, and Tavo, who cannot count, pulls at the belt to make the knots fly. When the last knot is loosed, the year is done, and we tie a new belt on our wrists and begin.
output.finding: Start at the Lamp-Petrel in the north and go a fist and a half straight south, where the Knot Belt hangs across the road.
